research_question: Compute historical monthly and annual mean streamflow statistics for the Red River of the North at Wahpeton, ND, up through water year 2009.

phase_1.user_prompt: I want to compile streamflow statistics for the Red River of the North at Wahpeton, North Dakota. Can you find the USGS site number for this location and identify the parameter code for daily mean discharge?

phase_2.user_prompt: Using the site number (05051500) and parameter for daily mean discharge (00060), download the complete daily streamflow record available up through the end of Water Year 2009 (September 30, 2009).

phase_3.user_prompt: Hydrologists often use the 'water year' (October 1 to September 30) for annual statistics. Using the daily data, calculate the mean monthly discharge for October of Water Year 1977 (which corresponds to calendar dates October 1-31, 1976). What is this monthly mean value in cubic feet per second?

phase_4.user_prompt: Now compute the annual mean discharge for every water year in the dataset. What is the overall grand mean of these annual mean discharges across the entire period of record used (through water year 2009)? Also, create a time series plot showing the annual mean discharge by water year and save it as `wahpeton_annual_mean_discharge.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The visualization should be a line or bar plot showing the annual mean discharge for the Red River of the North at Wahpeton over time, ending in water year 2009. The y-axis should represent discharge in cubic feet per second (cfs) and the x-axis should represent the water year. The plot should capture significant variability, with peak years like 2009 reaching over 1,800 cfs, and dry years like 1977 dipping very low.
checkpoint.visual_description: A time series line or scatter plot with 'Water Year' on the x-axis and 'Annual Mean Discharge (cfs)' on the y-axis, ending at 2009. Expected range spans from roughly 50 cfs to over 1800 cfs.
